technical_and_design_decisions: Implement acceptance tests at the public module interfaces without modifying production behavior unless a test exposes an actual defect.
Reuse the repository's existing build, test, naming, and assertion conventions.

Use deterministic local test doubles or embedded services for external protocols: an embedded mail server for Mail, local sockets for reactor-ip and syslog, an embedded SFTP server for SFTP, and a local HTTP mock server for http-client.
Use representative fixed fixtures for aggregator, bridge, and analytic-pmml scenarios so tests remain repeatable in CI.
Make tests isolated, independently runnable, and free of shared mutable state.
Register all new acceptance tests in the existing CI test lifecycle so they execute on every CI build.
Include negative-path and basic error-handling assertions in addition to successful end-to-end scenarios.
assumptions: The existing source repository, build system, and test framework are available and operational.
Existing module APIs and acceptance-test conventions are sufficiently documented to implement tests without production redesign.
Java 17 or later is available for local development and CI.
Adding test-scoped dependencies and test fixtures is permitted.
CI has network access to resolve dependencies, but the tests must not require external mail, SFTP, syslog, HTTP, or PMML services.
The increment requires coverage for the eight named modules only and does not require a full functional test of unrelated modules.
No cross-version, cross-operating-system, performance, security, or compatibility test matrix is required.
Effort includes implementation, local verification, CI configuration, and defect correction, but excludes waiting time for CI queues and external reviews.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the module structure, existing test harnesses, build configuration, CI workflow, supported APIs, and conventions for fixtures and test execution.
Define reusable setup and teardown utilities, local service fixtures, test data organization, port allocation, logging, and failure diagnostics for the eight module test suites.

Implement acceptance scenarios for receiving or processing mail through the Mail source, including representative message content, successful delivery, relevant metadata, and an error or boundary case.
Implement acceptance scenarios using local IP communication, covering connection or message ingestion, payload propagation, lifecycle behavior, and a representative failure case.
Implement acceptance scenarios for receiving syslog messages, validating parsed or propagated fields, handling representative message formats, and checking invalid or incomplete input behavior.

Implement acceptance scenarios against an embedded SFTP server, including file discovery or retrieval, content validation, post-processing behavior where applicable, and connection or missing-file handling.
Implement end-to-end tests for message grouping and aggregation, completion behavior, output validation, correlation or release conditions, and an incomplete or timeout-related case where supported.
Implement acceptance tests using representative PMML and input fixtures, validating successful model evaluation, mapped output values, and invalid or unsupported input handling.
Implement end-to-end tests proving messages pass through the bridge between the relevant endpoints without unintended transformation, including lifecycle and failure behavior.

Implement acceptance scenarios against a local HTTP mock service, covering request construction, response mapping, headers or payload handling, HTTP error responses, and timeout or connection failure behavior.
Configure the build and CI workflow to discover and execute all new acceptance suites on every CI build, including required test-scoped dependencies and service setup.

activities.activity_name: Local execution, stabilization, and defect correction
activities.activity_description: Run the complete suite repeatedly, diagnose flaky or environment-sensitive behavior, correct test and fixture issues, and perform focused regression checks across all affected modules.
Document how to run the acceptance suites locally, explain fixture or service prerequisites, and record any known limitations or maintenance guidance.
